tech_stack.rationale: SQLite rather than PostgreSQL so the whole project runs with no external service: a fixture that needs a database server running is a fixture that fails for reasons unrelated to what is being tested. No template is referenced, so Layer 0 creates directories rather than copying a tree from elsewhere.
tech_stack.notes: Backend only - no frontend, no container runtime.

api_endpoints.purpose: Accept a url and an optional title, store the link, and return the stored record including its generated id and created_at timestamp.
api_endpoints.inference_basis: The <description> states a POST endpoint accepting a URL and optional title. Method and behaviour are stated; the path string is inferred from the Link entity name. No /api prefix - the PRD never mentions one.

api_endpoints.purpose: Return every saved link as a JSON array, newest first by created_at. No pagination. Optionally filtered to a single tag.
api_endpoints.inference_basis: list-links criterion 1 names 'GET /links' verbatim. tag-links criterion 3 requires a tag filter on 'the list endpoint' without naming path or parameter. Merged into one endpoint - see merge_notes[1].

api_endpoints.purpose: Attach one or more tags to an existing link. Idempotent for tags already attached. 404 when the link id does not exist.
api_endpoints.inference_basis: Criteria 1, 2 and 4 describe posting tags to an existing link; the path shape is not stated in the feature.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a link is posted with a url and a title, the system shall store it and return 201 with an integer id, the submitted url and title, and a created_at timestamp.
When a link is posted with a url and no title, the system shall store it with a null title and return 201.
If a link is posted with no url field, then the system shall return 422 and store nothing.
If a link is posted with a url that does not parse as an absolute http or https URL, then the system shall return 422 and store nothing.
The system shall return 200 and a JSON array from GET /links, empty when no links are stored.
The system shall order listed links most recently created first.
The system shall include every stored link in the listing, reporting a null title rather than omitting an untitled link.
If the stored links cannot be read, then the system shall return 500 and shall not return an empty array, so that a failure to read is never reported as an empty shelf.
acceptance_criteria.note: No derived-from attribute in the source file. Recorded as absent, not back-filled.

acceptance_criteria.text: When tags are posted to an existing link, the system shall attach them and return 200 with the link reporting every attached tag.
When a tag already attached to a link is posted again, the system shall return 200 and leave the tag attached exactly once.
When links are listed with a tag filter, the system shall return exactly the links carrying that tag.
If tags are posted to a link id that does not exist, then the system shall return 404 and create no tag rows.

gaps.body: Whether a tag with no remaining links is deleted or kept is undecided. Keeping them makes an autocomplete list easy and lets the list rot.
gaps.note: Carried verbatim. NOT resolved. No detach/cleanup endpoint and no cascade or retention field was emitted, so the orphan-tag decision does not leak into the merged models or API surface.

merge_notes.detail: The index pass's keyword table maps 'Python + FastAPI' to `webapps/backends/python`, and the forked analyser initially emitted that path with provides [api_framework, orm, testing]. The PRD's own <rationale> disclaims it outright: 'No template is referenced, so Layer 0 creates directories rather than copying a tree from elsewhere.' Merged value is null. Had the keyword answer survived, Layer 0 would have been told to copy a tree the PRD says does not exist.

Two feature passes independently produced a listing endpoint: list-links inferred `GET /links` (its criterion 1 names the path verbatim) and tag-links inferred `GET /links?tag={tag}` from its criterion 3, which refers only to 'the list endpoint'. Neither pass could see the other. Merged to ONE endpoint, `GET /links` with an optional `tag` query parameter, attributed to both. Keeping them separate would have produced two tasks writing the same route handler.

Link is declared by save-link (owner), read by list-links (which explicitly declares it owns no entity and adds no column), and referenced by tag-links as LinkTag's FK target. All three attributions kept. Only save-link's task set creates the model; the other two must not re-declare it.

Every endpoint task's verification is pytest against the FastAPI app, which on FastAPI 0.110+/starlette means TestClient, which requires httpx at runtime. No feature declared it and the index's <dependencies> block does not list it. Added here because it is a mechanical consequence of the declared stack plus the declared test policy, not a product decision. Flagged rather than assumed: if the intended test style is ASGI transport via httpx.AsyncClient directly, the dependency is the same one.

architecture.md declares a layer named `frontend` (id 2). The index states 'Backend only - no frontend, no container runtime' and no feature pass produced a single component. Merged value is the empty list. The declared layer says the tier EXISTS in this project's graph; it is not evidence that THIS work puts anything in it. Layer derivation drops it - see layer_plan.json.

tag-links' <notes><considerations> states 'Tag names are matched case-sensitively.' That is behaviour an implementer needs, but considerations are unread by design and it is NOT an acceptance criterion. Not promoted to one here. Carried into task context as a constraint attributed to considerations, never as a criterion with an id.
One gap across three features: tag-links#1, kind=decision, blocking. Carried verbatim and unanswered.
